draft.text: You came to see us because your back pain has gotten worse.
It is in your lower back and goes down your left leg.
You have been using a cane because it is hard to stand for long periods.
We did not do any tests or exams during this visit.
However, you told us that an MRI showed a disk herniation at the L4-5 level.
This means a disk in your lower back is pressing on a nerve.
Your symptoms may be caused by a disk herniation at the L4-5 level.
This can lead to pain, weakness, and foot dragging.
You mentioned you had a fall off a roof 30 years ago, but you did not have surgery then.
We will ask your primary care doctor or the radiologist to check if spinal stenosis is present at the L4-5 level.
We also want to know which specific nerve roots are affected by the herniation.

unverified_summary.text: You came in because your back pain has gotten worse over time.
The pain is in your lower back and goes down your left leg.
It feels like an electrical toothache and is very strong, up to 13 out of 10 when it's worst.
You use a cane because it's hard to stand for long periods.
You had a fall off a roof 30 years ago, which might have caused a back injury.
You're having weakness in both legs and drag your foot when walking.
Your doctor thinks the pain may be from a disk pressing on a nerve in your lower back.
The doctor will check with your primary care doctor or a radiologist to see if there is spinal narrowing at the L4-5 level.
They will also find out which nerve is affected by the disk problem.
The next steps will be discussed after getting more information.
